Column selection across successive fetches differs from grouping all rows under nonunique keys.
One reused PDORow view differs from grouped arrays preserving repeated keys; the former demonstrates identity aliasing, not grouping policy.

Month arithmetic overflow and ISO week-year choice require distinct calendar rules and different failing dates.

Readonly's default protected setter scope allows one child initialization; asymmetric private(set) rejection concerns an ordinary property's restricted setter and partial writes.

Iterable admission tests arrays and Traversable versus Countable-only objects; scalar admission tests primitive PHP type categories. The interface boundary is essential only in 0471.
A clone hook changes a newly copied object; Closure::call temporarily changes the receiver without cloning it.
never is a covariant bottom return type that cannot return normally; nullable fallthrough is a missing explicit return. Different type and control-flow obligations.

Calendar month selection and grapheme-boundary slicing share only a failing-prefix test form.

A PDO lazy view is reused by fetch; a clone hook constructs a different object and does not rerun a constructor. Shared words about object state do not share the mechanism.
Failed mapping preserves the old assignment target because the RHS never completes; regex callback text semantics can be observed with successful pure calls and no failure.
Short-circuit evaluation controls which input reaches a throwing predicate; arrow capture controls whether outer state is mutated. Both callbacks are valid but differ for separate reasons.

Filtering requires correct callback parameter order and preserves selected keys; chunking partitions entries and separately chooses whether inner keys survive.
Fiber termination/getReturn is unrelated to evaluating match conditions and only the chosen result expression.
Binary framing chooses integer width, byte order and payload byte count; HMAC output encoding chooses raw digest bytes rather than hexadecimal text before base64.

Last-byte lookup uses zero-based length; negative-offset assignment also changes the string while retaining its length. Retain as read/write contrast, not a second identical index exercise.
define's success result is documented normal behavior; missing keyed destructuring emits a diagnostic and assigns null. Both discuss assigned values but expose different APIs.

Both close a session, mutate only local SESSION state, then reopen and lose the change. The same repair and timing rule decide both. Preserve IDs/objectives pending retain/retarget decision.
